sentences.zh: 高句麗 百濟 勿吉 失韋 豆莫婁 地豆于 庫莫奚 契丹 烏洛侯

translations.literal: Goguryeo, Baekje, Wuji, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didouyu, Kumo Xi, Khitan, Wuluohou
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo, Baekje, Wuji, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didouyu, Kumo Xi, Khitan, and Wuluohou

sentences.zh: 高句麗者，出於夫餘，自言先祖朱蒙。

translations.literal: Goguryeo sprang from Buyeo; they say their founding ancestor was Jumong.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Goguryeo came forth from Buyeo and claim Jumong as their founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙母河伯女，為夫餘王閉於室中，為日所照，引身避之，日影又逐。

translations.literal: Jumong's mother was a daughter of the River Lord; the king of Buyeo shut her in a chamber, the sun shone upon her, she drew her body away to avoid it, and the sun's shadow pursued again.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong's mother was a daughter of the River Lord. The king of Buyeo had shut her in a chamber; when sunlight fell upon her, she drew back to avoid it, yet the sun's shadow followed her still.

sentences.zh: 既而有孕，生一卵，大如五升。

translations.literal: Thereafter she became pregnant and bore an egg as large as five sheng.
translations.idiomatic: She soon conceived and gave birth to an egg as large as a five-sheng measure.

sentences.zh: 夫餘王棄之與犬，犬不食；

translations.literal: The king of Buyeo cast it away to a dog; the dog would not eat it.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Buyeo cast it out to a dog, but the dog would not touch it.

sentences.zh: 棄之與豕，豕又不食；

translations.literal: He cast it away to a pig; the pig again would not eat it.
translations.idiomatic: He cast it out to a pig, and the pig likewise refused it.

sentences.zh: 棄之於路，牛馬避之；

translations.literal: He cast it away on the road; oxen and horses shunned it.
translations.idiomatic: He left it on the road, and cattle and horses turned aside from it.

sentences.zh: 後棄之野，眾鳥以毛茹之。

translations.literal: Later he cast it away in the wilds; many birds warmed it with their feathers.
translations.idiomatic: At last he abandoned it in the wild, where flock upon flock of birds covered it with their feathers to warm it.

sentences.zh: 夫餘王割剖之，不能破，遂還其母。

translations.literal: The king of Buyeo cut and split it but could not break it open, and so returned it to its mother.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Buyeo tried to cut it open but could not break the shell, and so returned the egg to its mother.

sentences.zh: 其母以物裹之，置於暖處，有一男破殼而出。

translations.literal: His mother wrapped it in cloth and placed it in a warm place; a boy broke the shell and came forth.
translations.idiomatic: His mother wrapped it in cloth and set it in a warm place, until a boy broke the shell and emerged.

sentences.zh: 及其長也，字之曰朱蒙，其俗言「朱蒙」者，善射也。

translations.literal: When he had grown, they styled him Jumong; in their custom the word "Jumong" means skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: When he had grown to manhood they gave him the style Jumong, which in their tongue means one skilled in archery.

sentences.zh: 夫餘人以朱蒙非人所生，將有異志，請除之，王不聽，命之養馬。

translations.literal: The people of Buyeo, because Jumong was not born of a man, thought he would harbor a different intent and asked that he be put to death; the king would not listen and ordered him to raise horses.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Buyeo held that Jumong, not being born of mortal seed, would harbor rebellious designs, and asked that he be killed. The king refused and set him to raising horses instead.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙每私試，知有善惡，駿者減食令瘦，駑者善養令肥。

translations.literal: Jumong each time privately tested them and knew which were good and which bad; the swift he reduced in feed to make lean, the dull he well tended to make fat.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong would secretly test the horses and judge which were sound and which were not: he cut the rations of the swift so they grew lean, while he fed and cared for the slow until they grew fat.

sentences.zh: 夫餘王以肥者自乘，以瘦者給朱蒙。

translations.literal: The king of Buyeo rode the fat ones himself and gave the lean ones to Jumong.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Buyeo kept the fat horses for himself and gave Jumong only the lean ones.

sentences.zh: 後狩于田，以朱蒙善射，限之一矢。

translations.literal: Later on a hunt in the fields, because Jumong was skilled in archery, they limited him to one arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a hunt in the countryside, they allowed Jumong only a single arrow because of his renown as an archer.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙雖矢少，殪獸甚多。

translations.literal: Though Jumong had few arrows, the beasts he slew were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Though his arrows were few, Jumong brought down a great many beasts.

sentences.zh: 夫餘之臣又謀殺之。

translations.literal: The ministers of Buyeo again plotted to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of Buyeo again conspired to kill him.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙母陰知，告朱蒙曰：「國將害汝，以汝才略，宜遠適四方。

translations.literal: Jumong's mother knew in secret and told Jumong: "The state is about to harm you; given your talent and stratagem, you ought to flee far to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong's mother learned of the plot in secret and warned him, "The realm is about to destroy you. With your talent and resourcefulness, you should flee far beyond its borders.

sentences.zh: 」朱蒙乃與烏引、烏違等二人，棄夫餘，東南走。

translations.literal: " Jumong then, with Wuyin, Wuwei, and two others, abandoned Buyeo and fled southeast.
translations.idiomatic: " Jumong then left Buyeo with Wuyin, Wuwei, and two companions and fled southeast.

sentences.zh: 中道遇一大水，欲濟無梁，夫餘人追之甚急。

translations.literal: Midway they met a great river; they wished to cross but there was no bridge, and the men of Buyeo pursued them very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: On the way they came to a great river. They wished to cross but found no bridge, while the men of Buyeo pressed close behind.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙告水曰：「我是日子，河伯外孫，今日逃走，追兵垂及，如何得濟？

translations.literal: Jumong addressed the water: "I am a son of the sun, grandson of the River Lord; today I flee, the pursuers are almost upon me—how may I cross?
translations.idiomatic: Jumong cried to the river, "I am a son of the sun and grandson of the River Lord. Today I flee for my life, and the pursuers are almost upon me. How am I to cross?

sentences.zh: 」於是魚鼈並浮，為之成橋，朱蒙得渡，魚鼈乃解，追騎不得渡。

translations.literal: " Thereupon fish and turtles all floated up and formed a bridge for him; Jumong was able to cross, the fish and turtles then dispersed, and the pursuing horsemen could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: " At once fish and turtles rose together and formed a bridge. Jumong crossed safely; when the creatures dispersed, the pursuing horsemen could not follow.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙遂至普述水，遇見三人，其一人著麻衣，一人著納衣，一人著水藻衣，與朱蒙至紇升骨城，遂居焉，號曰高句麗，因以為氏焉。

translations.literal: Jumong then reached the Pusu River and met three men, one wearing hemp cloth, one wearing coarse cloth, and one wearing waterweed cloth; with Jumong they came to Kesunggu City, settled there, and took the name Goguryeo, using it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Jumong came at last to the Pusu River, where he met three men—one clad in hemp, one in coarse cloth, one in garments of waterweed. Together they went to Kesunggu City and made their home there, taking the name Goguryeo as their state and clan.

sentences.zh: 初，朱蒙在夫餘時，妻懷孕，朱蒙逃後生一子，字始閭諧。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Jumong was still in Buyeo, his wife was pregnant; after Jumong fled she bore a son, styled Shilüxie.
translations.idiomatic: While Jumong was still in Buyeo, his wife had been with child. After he fled she gave birth to a son, whom she styled Shilüxie.

sentences.zh: 及長，知朱蒙為國主，即與母亡而歸之，名之曰閭達，委之國事。

translations.literal: When he had grown, learning that Jumong was lord of the state, he fled with his mother to join him; he was named Lüda and entrusted with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the boy had grown, he learned that Jumong had become king and fled with his mother to join him. Jumong named him Lüda and entrusted him with the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 朱蒙死，閭達代立。

translations.literal: When Jumong died, Lüda succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jumong died, Lüda succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 閭達死，子如栗代立。

translations.literal: When Lüda died, his son Yuli succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Lüda died, his son Yuli took the throne.

sentences.zh: 如栗死，子莫來代立，乃征夫餘，夫餘大敗，遂統屬焉。

translations.literal: When Yuli died, his son Molai succeeded; he then campaigned against Buyeo, Buyeo suffered a great defeat, and he brought it under his rule.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuli died, his son Molai succeeded and marched against Buyeo. Buyeo was routed, and Molai brought it under his rule.

sentences.zh: 莫來子孫相傳，至裔孫宮，生而開目能視，國人惡之。

translations.literal: Molai's descendants passed the throne in succession down to a distant descendant Gong, who at birth opened his eyes and could see; the people of the state hated this.
translations.idiomatic: Molai's line held the throne in succession until a distant descendant named Gong was born with his eyes already open. The people regarded this as an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 及長凶虐，國以殘破。

translations.literal: When he had grown he was fierce and cruel, and the state was thereby ruined.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he proved fierce and cruel, and the realm fell into ruin.

sentences.zh: 宮曾孫位宮亦生而視，人以其似曾祖宮，故名為位宮，高句麗呼相似為「位」。

translations.literal: Gong's great-great-grandson Weigong also was born able to see; because men thought him like his great-great-grandfather Gong, he was therefore named Weigong; Goguryeo calls resemblance "wei."
translations.idiomatic: Gong's great-great-grandson Weigong was likewise born with his eyes open. Because he resembled his forebear Gong, he was named Weigong—the Goguryeo word wei meaning "to resemble."

sentences.zh: 位宮亦有勇力，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Weigong also had courage and strength and was skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong too was brave and strong, and adept with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 魏正始中，入寇遼西安平，[1]為幽州刺史毋丘儉所破。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era of Wei he invaded Liaoxi's Anping;[1] he was defeated by Guanqiu Jian, Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Wei's Zhengshi era he raided Anping in Liaoxi[1] and was defeated by Guanqiu Jian, Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 其玄孫乙弗利，利子釗，烈帝時與慕容氏相攻擊。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandson Yifuli had a son Chao; in the time of Emperor Lie they and the Murong clan attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandson Yifuli was succeeded by his son Chao, who in the reign of Emperor Lie waged war with the Murong.

sentences.zh: 建國四年，慕容元真率眾伐之，入自南陝，戰於木底，大破釗軍，乘勝長驅，遂入丸都，釗單馬奔竄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianguo, Murong Yuanzhen led his host against him, entering from Nanshan, fought at Mudi, routed Chao's army, pressed the victory in a long drive, entered Wandu, and Chao fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianguo, Murong Yuanzhen led an army against him, entering by the southern pass. At Mudi he routed Chao's forces, drove deep in pursuit, and entered Wandu while Chao fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 元真掘釗父墓，載其屍，并掠其母妻、珍寶、男女五萬餘口，焚其宮室，毀丸都城而還。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen dug up Chao's father's tomb and carried off the corpse, and together plundered his mother, wife, treasures, and more than fifty thousand men and women, burned the palaces, destroyed Wandu city, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen opened Chao's father's tomb and carried off the corpse, together with Chao's mother and wife, his treasures, and more than fifty thousand captives. He burned the palaces, razed Wandu, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自後釗遣使來朝，阻隔寇讎，不能自達。

translations.literal: From then on Chao sent envoys to court, but blocked by enemies and foes they could not reach on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Chao sent envoys to court, but enemies and warfare barred the way and they could not arrive.

sentences.zh: 釗後為百濟所殺。

translations.literal: Later Chao was killed by Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was later killed by Baekje.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，釗曾孫璉始遣使者安東奉表貢方物，并請國諱。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizu, Chao's great-grandson Lian first sent the envoy Andong to present a memorial and tribute of local products, and also requested the state's taboo names.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Shizu, Chao's great-grandson Lian first sent the envoy Andong with a memorial and local tribute, and asked to receive the imperial taboo names.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉其誠款，詔下帝系名諱於其國，遣員外散騎侍郎李敖拜璉為都督遼海諸軍事、征東將軍、領護東夷中郎將、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizu praised his sincerity, ordered the imperial lineage and taboo names sent down to his state, and dispatched Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant Li Ao to invest Lian as Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Liaohai, General Who Conquers the East, Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke Who Founded the State of Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his sincerity, sent down the imperial lineage and taboo names, and dispatched Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant Li Ao to invest Lian as Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Liaohai, General Who Conquers the East, Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 敖至其所居平壤城，訪其方事，云：遼東南一千餘里，東至柵城，南至小海，北至舊夫餘，民戶參倍於前。

translations.literal: Ao reached his seat at Pyongyang city and inquired into local affairs; it was said: south of Liaodong more than a thousand li, east to Zhacheng, south to the Lesser Sea, north to old Buyeo—the registered households were several times what they had been before.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ao reached Lian's capital at Pyongyang and inquired into local conditions, he learned that the realm stretched more than a thousand li south of Liaodong, east to Zhacheng, south to the Lesser Sea, and north to old Buyeo, with registered households several times greater than before.

sentences.zh: 魏時，其地東西二千里，南北一千餘里。

translations.literal: In the time of Wei its territory was two thousand li east to west and more than a thousand li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei times its territory measured two thousand li from east to west and more than a thousand li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 民皆土著，隨山谷而居，衣布帛及皮。

translations.literal: The people were all settled natives who dwelt along valleys and hills and wore cloth, silk, and fur.
translations.idiomatic: The people were all native settlers who lived along valleys and hills and dressed in cloth, silk, and hides.

sentences.zh: 土田薄塉，蠶農不足以自供，故其人節飲食。

translations.literal: The soil and fields were thin and poor; sericulture and farming were insufficient for self-supply, and so the people were sparing in food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: The land was thin and poor, and sericulture and farming could not fully sustain them, so the people were sparing in what they ate and drank.

sentences.zh: 其俗淫，好歌舞，夜則男女羣聚而戲，無貴賤之節，然潔淨自喜。

translations.literal: Their custom was licentious; they loved song and dance; at night men and women gathered in groups to sport without distinction of noble and base, yet they delighted in cleanliness.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were loose: they loved song and dance, and at night men and women would gather in groups to revel without regard to rank, though they took pride in cleanliness.

sentences.zh: 其王好治宮室。

translations.literal: Their king loved to build palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Their king delighted in building palaces.

sentences.zh: 其官名有謁奢、太奢、大兄、小兄之號。

translations.literal: Their official titles included Yeshe, Taishe, Da Xiong, and Xiao Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Among their offices were the titles Yeshe, Taishe, Da Xiong, and Xiao Xiong.

sentences.zh: 頭著折風，其形如弁，旁插鳥羽，貴賤有差。

translations.literal: On the head they wore zhefeng, shaped like a cap, with bird feathers inserted at the side, differing by noble and base rank.
translations.idiomatic: They wore on the head a zhefeng cap shaped like a formal crown, with bird feathers set in at the sides in grades according to rank.

sentences.zh: 立則反拱，跪拜曳一脚，行步如走。

translations.literal: When standing they folded their arms behind them; in bowing and kneeling they dragged one foot; in walking their steps were like running.
translations.idiomatic: When they stood they folded their arms behind their backs; when they bowed and knelt they dragged one foot; when they walked their gait was almost a run.

sentences.zh: 常以十月祭天，國中大會。

translations.literal: They regularly in the tenth month sacrificed to Heaven, and the state held a great assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the tenth month they sacrificed to Heaven, and the whole realm gathered in celebration.

sentences.zh: 其公會，衣服皆錦繡，金銀以為飾。

translations.literal: At their public assemblies their garments were all brocade and embroidery, with gold and silver for ornament.
translations.idiomatic: At their public assemblies all wore brocade and embroidery adorned with gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 好蹲踞。

translations.literal: They loved to squat.
translations.idiomatic: They were fond of squatting.

sentences.zh: 食用俎几。

translations.literal: In eating they used platters and low tables.
translations.idiomatic: They ate from platters set on low tables.

sentences.zh: 出三尺馬，云本朱蒙所乘，馬種即果下也。

translations.literal: They produced horses three feet high; it was said that originally Jumong had ridden them—the breed was the guoxia pony.
translations.idiomatic: They bred horses only three feet tall, said to be the same breed Jumong had ridden—the guoxia pony.

sentences.zh: 後貢使相尋，歲致黃金二百斤，白銀四百斤。

translations.literal: Later tribute envoys followed one after another; each year they presented two hundred jin of gold and four hundred jin of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute envoys came in steady succession, presenting two hundred jin of gold and four hundred jin of silver each year.

sentences.zh: 時馮文通率眾奔之，世祖遣散騎常侍封撥詔璉令送文通，璉上書稱當與文通俱奉王化，竟不送。

translations.literal: At that time Feng Wentong led his host in flight to them; Emperor Shizu sent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Feng Bo with an edict ordering Lian to hand over Wentong; Lian memorialized that he ought together with Wentong to submit to royal transformation, but in the end did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Feng Wentong fled to Goguryeo with his followers. The Emperor sent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Feng Bo with an edict ordering Lian to surrender him. Lian replied that he and Wentong would together accept the royal transform, but in the end he did not hand him over.

sentences.zh: 世祖怒，欲往討之，樂平王丕等議待後舉，世祖乃止，而文通亦尋為璉所殺。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizu was angry and wished to go punish them; the Prince of Leping Pi and others advised waiting for a later campaign, and the Emperor Shizu then stopped; Wentong before long was also killed by Lian.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and wished to march against them, but the Prince of Leping, Pi, and others urged delay, and he desisted. Before long Wentong was killed by Lian as well.

sentences.zh: 後文明太后以顯祖六宮未備，敕璉令薦其女。

translations.literal: Later Empress Dowager Wenming, because Emperor Xianzu's six palaces were not yet complete, ordered Lian to recommend his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Emperor Xianzu's inner palaces were not yet filled, Empress Dowager Wenming ordered Lian to present his daughter.

sentences.zh: 璉奉表，云女已出嫁，求以弟女應旨，朝廷許焉，乃遣安樂王真、尚書李敷等至境送幣。

translations.literal: Lian presented a memorial saying his daughter was already married and asked to use his younger brother's daughter to answer the decree; the court permitted it and then sent the Prince of Anle Zhen, Minister Li Fu, and others to the border to deliver betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Lian memorialized that his daughter was already married and asked to send his younger brother's daughter instead. The court agreed and dispatched the Prince of Anle, Zhen, Minister Li Fu, and others to the border with betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 璉惑其左右之說，云朝廷昔與馮氏婚姻，未幾而滅其國，殷鑒不遠，宜以方便辭之。

translations.literal: Lian was swayed by those about him, who said that formerly the court had taken a Feng in marriage and before long destroyed their state—the warning mirror was not far—and he ought by some expedient to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was swayed by his advisers, who said that when the court had once married a woman of the Feng clan, it had soon destroyed their state—a lesson not far in the past—and that he should find some polite excuse to refuse.

sentences.zh: 璉遂上書妄稱女死。

translations.literal: Lian then memorialized falsely claiming his daughter was dead.
translations.idiomatic: Lian then sent a false memorial claiming that the girl had died.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑其矯詐，又遣假散騎常侍程駿切責之，若女審死者，聽更選宗淑。

translations.literal: The court suspected deception and again sent Acting Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Cheng Jun to rebuke him sharply: if the daughter were truly dead, he was permitted to choose another clanswoman of good character.
translations.idiomatic: The court suspected fraud and sent Acting Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Cheng Jun to rebuke him sharply, adding that if the girl were truly dead he might select another suitable woman of the royal clan.

sentences.zh: 璉云：「若天子恕其前愆，謹當奉詔。

translations.literal: Lian said: "If the Son of Heaven pardons my former fault, I shall respectfully obey the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Lian replied, "If the Son of Heaven will pardon my former offense, I shall respectfully obey.

sentences.zh: 」會顯祖崩，乃止。

translations.literal: " It happened that Emperor Xianzu died, and the matter then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " But before anything further could be done, Emperor Xianzu died, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 至高祖時，璉貢獻倍前，其報賜亦稍加焉。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Gaozu, Lian's tribute was double what it had been before, and the rewards in return were also somewhat increased.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozu, Lian's tribute doubled what it had been, and the court's rewards in return grew somewhat as well.

sentences.zh: 時光州於海中得璉所遣詣蕭道成使餘奴等送闕，高祖詔責璉曰：「道成親殺其君，竊號江左，朕方欲興滅國於舊邦，繼絕世於劉氏，而卿越境外交，遠通篡賊，豈是藩臣守節之義！

translations.literal: At that time Guangzhou on the sea seized Lian's envoys sent to Xiao Daocheng, Yunu and others, and sent them to the palace; Emperor Gaozu edicted to rebuke Lian: "Daocheng personally killed his lord and usurped a title on the left of the Yangtze; We are just now wishing to raise up extinguished states in the old domains and continue the severed line of the Liu house, yet you cross borders in foreign relations and reach far to communicate with a usurping rebel—is this the meaning of a frontier subject keeping his integrity!
translations.idiomatic: At that time officials of Guangzhou seized at sea envoys Lian had sent to Xiao Daocheng, including Yunu, and brought them to court. Emperor Gaozu rebuked Lian: "Daocheng murdered his own sovereign and usurped rule south of the Yangtze. We mean to restore extinguished states and continue the house of Liu, yet you reach across the border to treat with a usurper. Is this how a frontier subject keeps faith?

sentences.zh: 今不以一過掩卿舊款，即送還藩，其感恕思愆，祗承明憲，輯寧所部，動靜以聞。」

translations.literal: Now We do not let one fault cover your former sincerity; return at once to your frontier; feel gratitude for pardon, reflect on your fault, respectfully receive the bright statutes, bring peace to your jurisdiction, and report your movements."
translations.idiomatic: We do not let a single fault efface your long loyalty. Return now to your realm, reflect on Our pardon, uphold the imperial statutes, keep your lands in order, and report all you do."

sentences.zh: 太和十五年，璉死，年百餘歲。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe, Lian died, aged more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Taihe, Lian died at more than a hundred years of age.

sentences.zh: 高祖舉哀於東郊，遣謁者僕射李安上策贈車騎大將軍、太傅、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu performed mourning at the eastern suburb and sent Gentlemen-attendant-in-Ordinary Li An to present a patent of posthumous investiture as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Tutor, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo, with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor performed mourning rites at the eastern suburb and sent Gentlemen-attendant-in-Ordinary Li An with a patent posthumously investing him as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Tutor, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo, with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 又遣大鴻臚拜璉孫雲使持節、都督遼海諸軍事、征東將軍、領護東夷中郎將、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王，賜衣冠服物車旗之飾，又詔雲遣世子入朝，令及郊丘之禮。

translations.literal: He also sent the Grand Herald to invest Lian's grandson Yun as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in Liaohai, General Who Conquers the East, Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo, granting robes, caps, garments, chariots, and banners, and also edicted Yun to send his heir to court in time for the suburban and mound rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the Grand Herald to invest Lian's grandson Yun with the same titles and regalia, and ordered Yun to send his heir to court in time for the suburban sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 雲上書辭疾，惟遣其從叔升于隨使詣闕，嚴責之。

translations.literal: Yun memorialized pleading illness and only sent his father's younger brother cousin Shengyu with the envoy to the palace; he was sternly rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Yun pleaded illness in a memorial and sent only his cousin Shengyu with the embassy. The court rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 自此歲常貢獻。

translations.literal: From then on tribute was presented every year.
translations.idiomatic: From that time tribute came every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 正始中，世宗於東堂引見其使芮悉弗，[2]悉弗進曰：「高麗係誠天極，累葉純誠，地產土毛，無愆王貢。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era, Emperor Shizong at the Eastern Hall received his envoy Ruixifu;[2] Xifu advanced and said: "Goryeo is bound in sincerity to the celestial pole, generation after generation pure in loyalty; the land produces local products and there is no fault in royal tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era, Emperor Shizong received the envoy Ruixifu in the Eastern Hall.[2] Ruixifu said, "Goryeo has bound itself in loyalty to Heaven, generation after generation, and the land yields its tribute without fail.

sentences.zh: 但黃金出自夫餘，珂則涉羅所產。

translations.literal: But gold came from Buyeo and ke-shell from Silla's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our gold came from Buyeo and our ke-shell from Silla's lands.

sentences.zh: 今夫餘為勿吉所逐，涉羅為百濟所并，國王臣雲惟繼絕之義，悉遷于境內。

translations.literal: Now Buyeo has been driven out by Wuji and Silla's territory taken by Baekje; the king your subject Yun, solely in the meaning of continuing the severed line, moved them all within his borders.
translations.idiomatic: Buyeo has now been driven out by the Wuji, and Silla's territory has been swallowed by Baekje. Our king Yun, upholding the duty to preserve severed lines, has taken all their people within our borders.

sentences.zh: 二品所以不登王府，實兩賊是為。

translations.literal: The reason the two grades of tribute do not reach the royal storehouse is truly because of these two marauders.
translations.idiomatic: It is solely because of these two enemies that the two grades of tribute no longer reach your treasury.

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「高麗世荷上將，專制海外，九夷黠虜，實得征之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong said: "Goryeo for generations has borne the grace of the supreme general and holds sole sway overseas; the crafty tribes of the nine Yi are in truth fit to be campaigned against.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor replied, "Goryeo has long enjoyed imperial favor and rules the seas beyond. The crafty tribes of the nine Yi are yours to subdue.

sentences.zh: 瓶罄罍耻，誰之咎也？

translations.literal: When the bottle is empty the jar is shamed—whose fault is it?
translations.idiomatic: When the bottle is empty the jar is shamed—whose fault is that?

sentences.zh: 昔方貢之愆，責在連率。

translations.literal: In former times fault in regional tribute lay with the regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when tribute failed, the fault lay with the regional commander.

sentences.zh: 卿宜宣朕旨於卿主，務盡威懷之略，揃披害羣，輯寧東裔，使二邑還復舊墟，土毛無失常貢也。」

translations.literal: You ought to proclaim Our intent to your lord, striving to exhaust the strategy of awe and cherishing, to sweep away harmful bands, bring peace to the eastern lands, and cause the two territories to return to their old mounds so that local products suffer no irregularity in tribute."
translations.idiomatic: You should convey Our intent to your king: employ both force and kindness, sweep away these enemies, restore peace to the eastern lands, and bring the two territories back to their old domains so that tribute may flow as before."

sentences.zh: 神龜中，雲死，靈太后為舉哀於東堂，遣使策贈車騎大將軍、領護東夷校尉、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era Yun died; Empress Dowager Ling performed mourning for him at the Eastern Hall and sent envoys with a patent posthumously investing him as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui era Yun died. Empress Dowager Ling performed mourning rites at the Eastern Hall and sent envoys posthumously investing him as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 又拜其世子安為安東將軍、領護東夷校尉、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王。

translations.literal: He also invested his heir An as General of Pacification of the East, Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: His heir An was invested as General of Pacification of the East, Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 正光初，光州又於海中執得蕭衍所授安寧東將軍衣冠劍佩，及使人江法盛等，送於京師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang, Guangzhou again on the sea seized the robes, cap, sword, and girdle ornaments that Xiao Yan had granted as General of Pacification and Tranquility of the East, together with his envoy Jiang Fasheng and others, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengguang, Guangzhou again seized at sea the regalia of General of Pacification and Tranquility of the East that Xiao Yan had granted, together with his envoy Jiang Fasheng and others, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 安死，子延立。

translations.literal: When An died, his son Yan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When An died, his son Yan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，詔加延使持節、散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、領護東夷校尉、遼東郡開國公、高句麗王，賜衣冠服物車旗之飾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu, an edict added for Yan Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo, granting robes, caps, garments, chariots, and banners.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Chu, Yan was further invested as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi, Duke Who Founded Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo, with full regalia.

sentences.zh: 天平中，詔加延侍中、驃騎大將軍，餘悉如故。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era an edict added for Yan Palace Attendant and General of Agile Cavalry; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was further named Palace Attendant and General of Agile Cavalry, his other titles remaining unchanged.

sentences.zh: 延死，子成立。

translations.literal: When Yan died, his son Cheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan died, his son Cheng took the throne.

sentences.zh: 訖於武定末，其貢使無歲不至。

translations.literal: Down to the end of Wuding there was no year in which tribute envoys did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the end of the Wuding era, tribute envoys came every year without exception.

sentences.zh: 百濟國，其先出自夫餘。

translations.literal: The state of Baekje: its forebears came forth from Buyeo.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Baekje traced its origins to Buyeo.

sentences.zh: 其國北去高句麗千餘里，處小海之南。

translations.literal: Its state lay more than a thousand li north from Goguryeo, situated south of the Lesser Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Its realm lay more than a thousand li south of Goguryeo, on the southern shore of the Lesser Sea.

sentences.zh: 其民土著，地多下濕，率皆山居。

translations.literal: Its people were settled natives; the land was largely low and wet, and for the most part they dwelt in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The people were native settlers on low, damp ground and for the most part lived in the hills.

sentences.zh: 有五穀，其衣服飲食與高句麗同。

translations.literal: They had the five grains; their clothing, food, and drink were the same as Goguryeo's.
translations.idiomatic: They grew the five grains, and their dress, food, and customs matched those of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 延興二年，其王餘慶始遣使上表曰：「臣建國東極，豺狼隔路，雖世承靈化，莫由奉藩，瞻望雲闕，馳情罔極。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanxing, its king Yuqing first sent envoys with a memorial saying: "Your subject founded his state at the eastern extremity; wolves and jackals block the road; though generation after generation we receive spiritual transformation, we have no means to submit as a frontier state; gazing toward the clouded gate-towers, our feelings race without limit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanxing, King Yuqing first sent envoys with a memorial: "Your subject founded his realm at the eastern edge of the world. Wolves block the road, and though we have received the imperial transform for generations, we have had no way to present ourselves at court. Gazing toward the celestial towers, our longing knows no bounds.

sentences.zh: 涼風微應，伏惟皇帝陛下協和天休，不勝係仰之情，謹遣私署冠軍將軍、駙馬都尉弗斯侯，長史餘禮，龍驤將軍、帶方太守、司馬張茂等投舫波阻，搜徑玄津，託命自然之運，遣進萬一之誠。

translations.literal: The cool wind lightly responds; we bow and consider that Your Majesty the Emperor harmonizes with Heaven's blessings; unable to bear the feeling of bound attachment, we respectfully send our privately appointed General of Champions, Commandant of the Majordomo's Stables the Marquis Fusi, Chief Clerk Yuli, General of the Dragon Courser Administrator of Daifang Zhang Mao and others, casting boats upon wave-blocked seas, searching paths through the dark ford, trusting fate to nature's course, to advance the slightest portion of our sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: As the cool wind stirs, we bow before Your Majesty, who harmonizes with Heaven's blessings. Unable to contain our devotion, we send our General of Champions and Commandant of the Majordomo's Stables, the Marquis Fusi, Chief Clerk Yuli, General of the Dragon Courser and Administrator of Daifang Zhang Mao, and others—casting their boats upon storm-tossed seas and searching out hidden routes—to bring, by Heaven's grace, the smallest measure of our loyalty.

sentences.zh: 冀神祇垂感，皇靈洪覆，克達天庭，宣暢臣志，雖旦聞夕沒，永無餘恨。

translations.literal: We hope the spirits and gods will incline in feeling, the imperial numen broadly cover us, that we may reach the celestial court, declare and fulfill your subject's intent—even hearing at dawn and perishing at dusk, forever without remaining regret.
translations.idiomatic: May the spirits incline to us and the imperial numen spread its shelter, that we may reach the celestial court and fulfill our purpose—even should we hear Your reply at dawn and die at dusk, we would have no regret remaining.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「臣與高句麗源出夫餘，先世之時，篤崇舊款。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Your subject and Goguryeo spring from the same source in Buyeo; in former generations we deeply honored old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "Your subject and Goguryeo alike spring from Buyeo, and in former ages we held each other in deep friendship.

sentences.zh: 其祖釗輕廢隣好，親率士眾，陵踐臣境。

translations.literal: Their ancestor Chao lightly cast aside neighborly friendship, personally led his soldiers and masses, and trampled and violated your subject's borders.
translations.idiomatic: Their ancestor Chao lightly cast aside our friendship, led his army in person, and trampled our borders.

sentences.zh: 臣祖須整旅電邁，應機馳擊，矢石暫交，梟斬釗首。

translations.literal: Your subject's ancestor Xu mustered his troops in lightning march, struck according to opportunity in swift attack; arrows and stones had barely crossed when Chao's head was taken and displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's ancestor Xu mustered his troops and struck like lightning. After a brief clash of arms he took Chao's head.

sentences.zh: 自爾已來，莫敢南顧。

translations.literal: From then until now none has dared to look southward.
translations.idiomatic: From that day none of them dared turn south again.

sentences.zh: 自馮氏數終，餘燼奔竄，醜類漸盛，遂見陵逼，構怨連禍，三十餘載，財殫力竭，轉自孱踧。

translations.literal: Since the Feng clan's number ended and the remaining embers fled in disorder, ugly sorts gradually grew strong, and we then suffered encroachment and bullying; grievance linked to calamity for more than thirty years; wealth exhausted and strength spent, we turned ever more feeble and cramped.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fall of the Feng clan and the flight of their remnants, vile enemies have grown strong and pressed upon us. Grievance has piled upon calamity for more than thirty years until our wealth is spent and our strength exhausted, and we grow ever weaker.

sentences.zh: 若天慈曲矜，遠及無外，速遣一將，來救臣國，當奉送鄙女，執掃後宮，并遣子弟，牧圉外廐。

translations.literal: If Heaven's compassion bends graciously and reaches far to exclude none, swiftly send one general to rescue your subject's state; your subject shall present his humble daughter to sweep the inner palace and also send sons and younger kin to tend the outer pastures and stables.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven shows mercy and extends its care to the farthest reaches, send a general at once to rescue my realm. I shall offer my humble daughter to serve in the inner palace and send my sons and younger kin to tend your outer stables.

sentences.zh: 尺壤匹夫不敢自有。

translations.literal: Not a foot of soil nor a single common man would your subject dare claim as his own.
translations.idiomatic: Not a foot of land nor a single subject would I dare hold as my own.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「今璉有罪，國自魚肉，大臣強族，戮殺無已，罪盈惡積，民庶崩離。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Now Lian is guilty; the state cuts itself like fish and meat; great ministers and powerful clans slaughter without end; crimes overflow and wickedness accumulates; the people scatter and fall away.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "Lian is guilty now. His realm tears itself apart like meat on a chopping block; powerful ministers and clans slaughter without end; crimes and wickedness pile high, and the people are scattering.

sentences.zh: 是滅亡之期，假手之秋也。

translations.literal: This is the season of extinction, the autumn for lending another's hand.
translations.idiomatic: The hour of their destruction has come—the season to strike by another's hand.

sentences.zh: 且馮族士馬，有鳥畜之戀；

translations.literal: Moreover the Feng clan's soldiers and horses still hold the longing of birds and beasts for their old nests.
translations.idiomatic: The Feng clan's warriors and horses still yearn for their old homeland, like birds and beasts for their nests.

sentences.zh: 樂浪諸郡，懷首丘之心。

translations.literal: The commanderies of Lelang harbor hearts that turn toward the mound of their heads.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Lelang commanderies still turn their hearts toward home.

sentences.zh: 天威一舉，有征無戰。

translations.literal: When Heaven's majesty moves once, there is campaign but no battle.
translations.idiomatic: One display of Heaven's majesty, and they will submit without a fight.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不敏，志效畢力，當率所統，承風響應。

translations.literal: Your subject, though not clever, is resolved to exhaust his strength and will lead those he commands to answer in echo to the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am not clever, I am resolved to give all my strength and will lead my followers to answer your call.

sentences.zh: 且高麗不義，逆詐非一，外慕隗囂藩卑之辭，內懷兇禍豕突之行。

translations.literal: Moreover Goryeo is unrighteous; its treachery and deceit are not one alone; outwardly it admires the humble words of a frontier subject like Wei Xiao, inwardly it harbors the conduct of violent disaster like a boar's rush.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo is faithless, and their treachery knows many forms: outwardly they mouth the humble phrases of a frontier vassal like Wei Xiao, while inwardly they plot violence like a charging boar.

sentences.zh: 或南通劉氏，或北約蠕蠕，共相脣齒，謀陵王略。

translations.literal: Sometimes they reach south to ally with the Liu house, sometimes north they treaty with the Rouran; they are lip and teeth to each other and plot to encroach on the royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: Now they treat with the Liu house in the south, now they pact with the Rouran in the north, standing lip to teeth with each ally as they plot against the imperial domain.

sentences.zh: 昔唐堯至聖，致罰丹水；

translations.literal: In old times even the supremely sage Emperor Yao of Tang inflicted punishment on the Dan River folk.
translations.idiomatic: Even the sage Emperor Yao of old punished the people of the Dan River.

sentences.zh: 孟常稱仁，不捨塗詈。

translations.literal: Meng Chang was called humane yet did not spare those who cursed him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang was famed for benevolence, yet he did not spare those who reviled him in the streets.

sentences.zh: 涓流之水，宜早壅塞，今若不取，將貽後悔。

translations.literal: A trickling stream ought early to be dammed; if now you do not take action, you will bequeath regret.
translations.idiomatic: A trickling stream should be dammed early. If you do not act now, you will regret it later.

sentences.zh: 去庚辰年後，臣西界小石山北國海中見屍十餘，并得衣器鞍勒，視之非高麗之物，後聞乃是王人來降臣國。

translations.literal: After the gengchen year, on the sea north of the small Stone Mountain at your subject's western border more than ten corpses were seen, together with clothing, vessels, saddles, and bridles; viewing them they were not Goryeo goods; later it was heard that they were men of the king's domain coming to submit to your subject's state.
translations.idiomatic: After the gengchen year, more than ten corpses were found in the sea north of Little Stone Mountain on my western border, together with clothing, gear, saddles, and bridles that were plainly not Goryeo goods. I later learned they were men of Your Majesty's realm seeking refuge in my country.

sentences.zh: 長蛇隔路，以沉于海，雖未委當，深懷憤恚。

translations.literal: A long serpent blocked the road and they sank in the sea; though the matter is not yet settled, your subject harbors deep indignation.
translations.idiomatic: A long serpent blocked their path and they perished in the sea. Though the facts are not yet clear, I am deeply aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 昔宋戮申舟，楚莊徒跣；

translations.literal: In old times Song killed Shen Zhou and King Zhuang of Chu went barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: When Song killed Shen Zhou, King Zhuang of Chu went barefoot in mourning.

sentences.zh: 鷂撮放鳩，信陵不食。

translations.literal: The sparrow hawk seized and then released the dove; Lord Xinling would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: The hawk seized the dove and then released it; Lord Xinling would not touch his meal.

sentences.zh: 克敵建名，美隆無已。

translations.literal: To overcome enemies and establish a name—such glory knows no end.
translations.idiomatic: To defeat one's foes and win renown is glory without end.

sentences.zh: 夫以區區偏鄙，猶慕萬代之信，況陛下合氣天地，勢傾山海，豈令小竪，跨塞天逵。

translations.literal: That a petty, remote, and vulgar land still yearns for faith lasting ten thousand generations—how much more Your Majesty, who shares the breath of Heaven and Earth and whose power tilts mountains and seas—could you allow a petty chieftain to block the heavenly thoroughfare?
translations.idiomatic: If even our small and remote realm still cherishes loyalty lasting ten thousand generations, how much more should Your Majesty, who shares the breath of Heaven and Earth and whose power overawes mountains and seas, permit a petty chieftain to block the road to Heaven?

sentences.zh: 今上所得鞍一，以為實驗。」

translations.literal: The saddle now presented above is offered as proof."
translations.idiomatic: The saddle I now present is offered as proof."

sentences.zh: 顯祖以其僻遠，冒險朝獻，禮遇優厚，遣使者邵安與其使俱還。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu, because they were remote and distant and had braved peril to come to court, treated them with generous courtesy and sent the envoy Shao An to return together with their embassy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu, moved that they had braved such distances to present tribute, received them with generous courtesy and sent the envoy Shao An to return with their embassy.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「得表聞之，無恙甚善。

translations.literal: An edict said: "We have received your memorial and learned of it; that you are without illness is very good.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "We have received your memorial and are pleased to learn you are well.

sentences.zh: 卿在東隅，處五服之外，不遠山海，歸誠魏闕，欣嘉至意，用戢于懷。

translations.literal: You are in the eastern corner, situated beyond the five degrees of mourning garb, not far from mountains and seas, returning in sincerity to the Wei gate-towers; We rejoice in your utmost intent and rest it in Our breast.
translations.idiomatic: You dwell in the far east, beyond the five domains, yet not so far from mountains and sea that you cannot turn in loyalty to the Wei court. We rejoice in your devotion and hold it close in Our heart.

sentences.zh: 朕承萬世之業，君臨四海，統御羣生。

translations.literal: We inherit the enterprise of ten thousand generations, rule as sovereign over the four seas, and govern all living beings.
translations.idiomatic: We inherit the enterprise of ten thousand generations, rule the four seas, and govern all living beings.

sentences.zh: 今宇內清一，八表歸義，襁負而至者不可稱數，風俗之和，士馬之盛，皆餘禮等親所聞見。

translations.literal: Now within the four quarters all is pure and unified, the eight directions return to righteousness, those who come carried in swaddling clothes cannot be numbered; the harmony of customs and the abundance of soldiers and horses—all this your subject Yuli and the others have themselves heard and seen.
translations.idiomatic: Within the four seas all is at peace, and from the eight directions subjects come in numbers beyond count. The harmony of customs and the strength of armies—your envoy Yuli and his companions have seen this with their own eyes.

sentences.zh: 卿與高麗不穆，屢致陵犯，苟能順義，守之以仁，亦何憂於寇讎也。

translations.literal: You and Goryeo are not harmonious and repeatedly suffer encroachment and violation; if you can follow righteousness and guard it with benevolence, what worry need you have of enemy foes?
translations.idiomatic: You and Goryeo are at odds and have suffered repeated encroachments. If you uphold righteousness and govern with benevolence, what enemy need you fear?

sentences.zh: 前所遣使，浮海以撫荒外之國，從來積年，往而不返，存亡達否，未能審悉。

translations.literal: Envoys formerly dispatched crossed the sea to comfort states beyond the wild frontier; for years they have gone and not returned; whether they live or die, succeed or fail, We have been unable to examine and know fully.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys We sent before crossed the sea to reach distant lands, and for years none have returned. Whether they live or die, succeed or fail, We have been unable to learn.

sentences.zh: 卿所送鞍，比校舊乘，非中國之物。

translations.literal: The saddle you sent, compared with Our old mounts, is not an object of the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: The saddle you sent, compared with Our own mounts, is plainly not of the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 不可以疑似之事，以生必然之過。

translations.literal: One must not from doubtful matters give rise to certain guilt.
translations.idiomatic: One must not turn doubtful evidence into certain guilt.

sentences.zh: 經略權要，已具別旨。

translations.literal: The essentials of strategy and authority have already been set forth in separate instructions.
translations.idiomatic: The essentials of strategy have been set forth in separate instructions.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「知高麗阻強，侵軼卿土，修先君之舊怨，棄息民之大德，兵交累載，難結荒邊。

translations.literal: " Another edict said: "We know that Goryeo, relying on its strength, encroaches upon and violates your lands, nurses old grievances of former rulers, abandons the great virtue of giving the people rest, and that arms have clashed for many years, making it hard to settle the wild frontier.
translations.idiomatic: " Another edict said, "We know that Goryeo, relying on its strength, encroaches on your lands, nurses old grievances, abandons the great virtue of giving the people peace, and that war has dragged on for years along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 使兼申胥之誠，國有楚越之急，乃應展義扶微，乘機電舉。

translations.literal: Your envoy combines the sincerity of Shen Xu; your state has the urgency of Chu and Yue; thus you ought to display righteousness and support the weak, seizing the moment in lightning action.
translations.idiomatic: Your envoy speaks with the sincerity of Wu Zixu, and your state faces the urgency of Chu and Yue. It is right that you should uphold righteousness, aid the weak, and strike like lightning when the moment comes.

sentences.zh: 但以高麗稱藩先朝，供職日久，於彼雖有自昔之釁，於國未有犯令之愆。

translations.literal: Yet Goryeo has called itself a frontier state to the former court and performed duties for a long time; toward them, though there are old grievances from of old, toward the state there is as yet no offense of violating orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Goryeo has long called itself a vassal of the former court and performed its duties. Though old grievances exist between you, it has not yet violated imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 卿使命始通，便求致伐，尋討事會，理亦未周。

translations.literal: Your mission has only just opened relations and at once you ask to launch a campaign; searching through the circumstances, the reasoning is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Your embassy has only just opened relations, yet you already ask for a campaign. When the matter is examined, the case is not yet complete.

sentences.zh: 故往年遣禮等至平壤，欲驗其由狀。

translations.literal: Therefore in former years We sent Li and others to Pyongyang to verify the origins of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in former years We sent Li and others to Pyongyang to verify the facts.

sentences.zh: 然高麗奏請頻煩，辭理俱詣，行人不能抑其請，司法無以成其責，故聽其所啟，詔禮等還。

translations.literal: Yet Goryeo's memorials and requests came frequently; its arguments and reasoning were both presented; the traveling envoys could not restrain its requests; the judicial offices had no means to fix its guilt; therefore We heard what it submitted and ordered Li and the others to return.
translations.idiomatic: But Goryeo's petitions came again and again with reasoned pleas. Our envoys could not silence their appeals, and the judicial offices could not establish guilt. We therefore heard their case and ordered Li and the others to return.

sentences.zh: 若今復違旨，則過咎益露，後雖自陳，無所逃罪，然後興師討之，於義為得。

translations.literal: If now they again disobey the edict, then fault and guilt will be further exposed; later, even if they plead on their own behalf, there will be no escaping punishment; only then to raise armies and punish them is righteous.
translations.idiomatic: If they now disobey Our edict again, their guilt will stand revealed. Even if they plead later, they cannot escape punishment, and only then will it be right to raise armies against them.

sentences.zh: 九夷之國，世居海外，道暢則奉藩，惠戢則保境，故羈縻著於前典，楛貢曠於歲時。

translations.literal: The states of the nine Yi for generations dwell beyond the sea; when the Way is open they submit as frontier states, when favor rests they guard their borders; therefore loose reins are recorded in former canons, and tribute of arrows has lapsed in its seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The states of the nine Yi have long dwelt beyond the sea: when the Way prevails they submit as vassals, when favor rests they keep their borders. Loose reins are recorded in the ancient canons, yet tribute has sometimes lapsed.

sentences.zh: 卿備陳強弱之形，具列往代之迹，俗殊事異，擬貺乖衷，洪規大略，其致猶在。

translations.literal: You fully set forth the forms of strength and weakness, completely listed the traces of former generations; customs differ and affairs vary, and your proposed gifts miss the mark, yet the great plan and broad outline—their intent still stands.
translations.idiomatic: You have fully described the balance of strength and weakness and traced the record of former ages. Customs differ and affairs vary, and some of your proposals miss the mark, yet the broad intent of your plan still stands.

sentences.zh: 今中夏平一，宇內無虞，每欲陵威東極，懸旌域表，拯荒黎於偏方，舒皇風於遠服。

translations.literal: Now the central Xia is unified and within the four quarters there is no worry; We constantly wish to extend majesty to the eastern extremity, plant banners beyond the borders, rescue wild peoples in remote corners, and spread the imperial wind to distant domains.
translations.idiomatic: Now the central lands are unified and the realm is at peace. We constantly wish to extend Our majesty to the eastern edge, plant banners beyond the borders, rescue distant peoples, and spread the imperial wind to far domains.

sentences.zh: 良由高麗即敍，未及卜征。

translations.literal: It is truly because Goryeo has just renewed relations that We have not yet divined a campaign.
translations.idiomatic: It is only because Goryeo has just renewed relations that We have not yet undertaken a campaign.

sentences.zh: 今若不從詔旨，則卿之來謀，載協朕意，元戎啟行，將不云遠。

translations.literal: If now they do not follow the edict, then your coming counsel matches Our intent; the great army will set forth, and it will not be said to be far.
translations.idiomatic: If they now disobey Our edict, your counsel will match Our intent, and the great army will march—not far off.

sentences.zh: 便可豫率同興，具以待事，時遣報使，速究彼情。

translations.literal: You may forthwith lead your forces to rise together in advance, make ready to await events, and from time to time send reporting envoys to swiftly investigate their situation.
translations.idiomatic: Prepare your forces to rise with Us, make ready for what is to come, and send envoys from time to time to report swiftly on their situation.

sentences.zh: 師舉之日，卿為鄉導之首，大捷之後，又受元功之賞，不亦善乎。

translations.literal: On the day the army is raised you shall be chief guide; after a great victory you shall again receive reward for the foremost merit—is this not good?
translations.idiomatic: When the army marches, you shall lead the way as chief guide; after a great victory you shall receive the foremost reward. Would that not be fitting?

sentences.zh: 所獻錦布海物雖不悉達，明卿至心。

translations.literal: The brocade, cloth, and sea products you presented, though not all arrived, make clear your utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The brocade, cloth, and sea products you presented, though not all arrived, show your utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 今賜雜物如別。

translations.literal: Now miscellaneous objects are granted as listed separately.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous gifts are granted as listed separately.

sentences.zh: 」又詔璉護送安等。

translations.literal: " Another edict ordered Lian to escort An and the others.
translations.idiomatic: " Another edict ordered Lian to escort An and his party.

sentences.zh: 安等至高句麗，璉稱昔與餘慶有讎，不令東過，安等於是皆還。

translations.literal: When An and the others reached Goguryeo, Lian said that in former times he had a feud with Yuqing and would not let them pass eastward; An and the others therefore all returned.
translations.idiomatic: When An and his party reached Goguryeo, Lian claimed an old feud with Yuqing and refused to let them pass eastward. They therefore all returned.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔切責之。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued sternly rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued sternly rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 五年，使安等從東萊浮海，賜餘慶璽書，褒其誠節。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, An and the others were sent from Donglai across the sea, and a sealed letter was granted to Yuqing praising his sincerity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, An and his party were sent from Donglai by sea with a sealed letter for Yuqing praising his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 安等至海濱，遇風飄蕩，竟不達而還。

translations.literal: When An and the others reached the seashore they met winds that tossed them about and in the end did not arrive but returned.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the coast, storms tossed them about, and in the end they could not arrive and returned.

sentences.zh: 勿吉國，在高句麗北，舊肅慎國也。

translations.literal: The state of Wuji lies north of Goguryeo; it is the old state of Sushen.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Wuji lies north of Goguryeo and is the old land of Sushen.

sentences.zh: 邑落各自有長，不相總一。

translations.literal: Each settlement and hamlet has its own chief and they are not united under one ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Each settlement has its own chief, and they are not united under one ruler.

sentences.zh: 其人勁悍，於東夷最強。

translations.literal: Its people are fierce and strong; among the Eastern Yi they are the most powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Their people are fierce and strong—the most powerful among the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 言語獨異。

translations.literal: Their language is uniquely different.
translations.idiomatic: Their language is wholly distinct.

sentences.zh: 常輕豆莫婁等國，諸國亦患之。

translations.literal: They constantly look down on the states of Doumolou and others; the various states also suffer from them.
translations.idiomatic: They constantly look down on Doumolou and the other states, which likewise suffer from their raids.

sentences.zh: 去洛五千里。

translations.literal: It is five thousand li from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It lies five thousand li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 自和龍北二百餘里有善玉山，山北行十三日至祁黎山，又北行七日至如洛瓌水，水廣里餘，又北行十五日至太魯水，又東北行十八日到其國。

translations.literal: From two hundred-odd li north of Helong is Mount Shanyu; going north from the mountain thirteen days reaches Mount Qili; going north again seven days reaches the Ruluohuan River, the river more than a li wide; going north again fifteen days reaches the Tailu River; going northeast again eighteen days reaches their state.
translations.idiomatic: Some two hundred li north of Helong stands Mount Shanyu. Thirteen days' travel north of the mountain brings one to Mount Qili; seven days farther north to the Ruluohuan River, more than a li across; fifteen days farther north to the Tailu River; and eighteen days northeast to their country.

sentences.zh: 國有大水，闊三里餘，名速末水。

translations.literal: The state has a great river more than three li wide, named the Sumo River.
translations.idiomatic: Their country has a great river more than three li wide called the Sumo River.

sentences.zh: 其地下濕，築城穴居，屋形似塚，開口於上，以梯出入。

translations.literal: Their land is low and wet; they build walled settlements and dwell in pits; their houses are shaped like mounds, with openings above, and they use ladders to enter and exit.
translations.idiomatic: The land is low and damp. They build walled settlements and live in pit dwellings shaped like burial mounds, entering and leaving by ladder through an opening above.

sentences.zh: 其國無牛，有車馬，佃則偶耕，車則步推。

translations.literal: Their state has no cattle; they have chariots and horses; in farming they plow in pairs, and for carts they push on foot.
translations.idiomatic: They have no cattle but do have horses and carts. They plow in pairs, and push their carts on foot.

sentences.zh: 有粟及麥穄，菜則有葵。

translations.literal: They have millet and wheat chaff; for vegetables they have mallow.
translations.idiomatic: They grow millet and wheat, and among vegetables they cultivate mallow.

sentences.zh: 水氣醎凝，鹽生樹上，亦有鹽池。

translations.literal: Water vapor turns salty and congeals; salt grows on trees, and there are also salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: Moisture turns brackish and congeals; salt forms on trees, and there are salt ponds as well.

sentences.zh: 多猪無羊。

translations.literal: They have many pigs and no sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They keep many pigs but have no sheep.

sentences.zh: 嚼米醞酒，飲能至醉。

translations.literal: They chew rice to brew wine; drinking can bring them to drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: They chew rice to brew wine and can drink themselves drunk.

sentences.zh: 婦人則布裙，男子猪犬皮裘。

translations.literal: Women wear cloth skirts; men wear furs of pig and dog.
translations.idiomatic: Women wear cloth skirts; men wear furs of pig and dog skin.

sentences.zh: 初婚之夕，男就女家執女乳而罷，便以為定，仍為夫婦。

translations.literal: On the first night of marriage the man goes to the woman's house, grasps the woman's breast and stops, and this is taken as the bond; they then become husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding night the groom goes to the bride's house, touches her breast, and the match is sealed; they then become husband and wife.

sentences.zh: 俗以人溺洗手面。

translations.literal: Their custom is to wash hands and face with human urine.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they wash their hands and face with human urine.

sentences.zh: 頭插虎豹尾。

translations.literal: In the hair they insert tails of tiger and leopard.
translations.idiomatic: They wear tiger and leopard tails in their hair.

sentences.zh: 善射獵，弓長三尺，箭長尺二寸，以石為鏃。

translations.literal: They are skilled in archery and hunting; bows are three feet long, arrows one foot two inches, with stone for arrowheads.
translations.idiomatic: They are skilled archers and hunters. Their bows are three feet long, their arrows a foot and two inches, with stone heads.

sentences.zh: 其父母春夏死，立埋之，冢上作屋，不令雨濕；

translations.literal: When their parents die in spring or summer they bury them at once, build a house atop the mound, and do not let rain dampen it.
translations.idiomatic: When parents die in spring or summer they bury them at once, build a house over the mound, and keep the rain off.

sentences.zh: 若秋冬，以其屍捕貂，貂食其肉，多得之。

translations.literal: If in autumn or winter, they use the corpse to catch sable; sable eat its flesh and they obtain many.
translations.idiomatic: If death comes in autumn or winter, they use the corpse to trap sable, which feed on the flesh and are caught in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 常七八月造毒藥傅箭鏃，射禽獸，中者便死，煮藥毒氣亦能殺人。

translations.literal: Regularly in the seventh or eighth month they make poison, smear it on arrowheads, and shoot birds and beasts; those struck die at once, and the vapor from boiling the poison can also kill men.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the seventh or eighth month they brew poison, smear it on arrowheads, and shoot game. Whatever is struck dies at once, and even the fumes from boiling the poison can kill a man.

sentences.zh: 國南有徒太山，魏言「大白」，有虎豹羆狼害人，人不得山上溲汙，行逕山者，皆以物盛。

translations.literal: South of the state is Mount Taitai; in Wei speech it is called "Great White." Tigers, leopards, bears, and wolves harm people; people may not relieve themselves on the mountain; those who travel paths on the mountain all carry vessels.
translations.idiomatic: South of their country stands Mount Taitai, called in Wei speech Great White. Tigers, leopards, bears, and wolves harm people. No one may relieve himself on the mountain; travelers carry vessels for that purpose.

sentences.zh: 去延興中，遣使乙力支朝獻。

translations.literal: In the Yanxing era an envoy Yilizhi was sent to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanxing era they sent the envoy Yilizhi to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 太和初，又貢馬五百匹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe they again presented five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era they presented five hundred horses in tribute.

sentences.zh: 乙力支稱：初發其國，乘船泝難河西上，至太𣳅河，沉船於水，南出陸行，渡洛孤水，從契丹西界達和龍。

translations.literal: Yilizhi said: When we first set out from our state we took boats up the Nahan River westward to the Taiyu River, sank the boats in the water, went south and traveled by land, crossed the Luogu River, and from the western border of the Khitan reached Helong.
translations.idiomatic: Yilizhi said that when they first set out they sailed up the Nahan River westward to the Taiyu River, sank their boats, continued south overland, crossed the Luogu River, and reached Helong by way of the Khitan western border.

sentences.zh: 自云其國先破高句麗十落，密共百濟謀從水道并力取高句麗，遣乙力支奉使大國，請其可否。

translations.literal: He said of himself that his state had first broken ten settlements of Goguryeo and secretly together with Baekje plotted to take Goguryeo by water route with combined strength; Yilizhi was sent as envoy to the great state to ask whether this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He said his people had first overrun ten Goguryeo settlements and were secretly plotting with Baekje to attack Goguryeo by water. Yilizhi was sent to the great state to ask whether this was permitted.

sentences.zh: 詔敕三國同是藩附，宜共和順，勿相侵擾。

translations.literal: An edict ordered: The three states are alike frontier subjects; they ought jointly to be harmonious and compliant and not encroach upon or harass one another.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied that all three states were imperial vassals and should live in harmony and not harass one another.

sentences.zh: 乙力支乃還。

translations.literal: Yilizhi then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yilizhi then returned home.

sentences.zh: 從其來道，取得本船，汎達其國。

translations.literal: By the route by which they had come they recovered their original boats and sailed across to reach their state.
translations.idiomatic: By the route they had taken, they recovered their original boats and sailed home.

sentences.zh: 九年，復遣使侯尼支朝獻。

translations.literal: In the ninth year an envoy Hounizhi was again sent to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year they again sent the envoy Hounizhi to court.

sentences.zh: 明年復入貢。

translations.literal: The next year they again entered with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they presented tribute again.

sentences.zh: 其傍有大莫盧國、覆鍾國、莫多回國、庫婁國、素和國、具弗伏國、[3]匹黎尒國、拔大何國、[4]郁羽陵國、庫伏真國、魯婁國、羽真侯國，前後各遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: Beside them are the states of Damolu, Fuzhong, Moduohui, Kulou, Suhe, Jufufu,[3] Pilier, Badahé,[4] Yuyuling, Kufuzhen, Lulou, and Yuzhenhou; each in turn sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby are the states of Damolu, Fuzhong, Moduohui, Kulou, Suhe, Jufufu,[3] Pilier, Badahé,[4] Yuyuling, Kufuzhen, Lulou, and Yuzhenhou, each of which sent envoys to court in its turn.

sentences.zh: 太和十二年，勿吉復遣使貢楛矢方物於京師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Taihe, Wuji again sent envoys to present tribute of bundled arrows and local products at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Taihe, Wuji again sent envoys to the capital with bundled arrows and local products.

sentences.zh: 十七年，又遣使人婆非等五百餘人朝獻。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year they again sent the envoy Renpofei and more than five hundred others to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year they sent the envoy Renpofei and more than five hundred followers to court.

sentences.zh: 景明四年，復遣使俟力歸等朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingming they again sent the envoy Houligui and others to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingming they again sent the envoy Houligui and others to court.

sentences.zh: 自此迄于正光，貢使相尋。

translations.literal: From then until Zhengguang tribute envoys followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: From then until Zhengguang, tribute envoys came in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 爾後，中國紛擾，頗或不至。

translations.literal: After that the Middle Kingdom was in turmoil and they often did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, as the central realm fell into turmoil, they often failed to come.

sentences.zh: 興和二年六月，遣使石久云等貢方物，至於武定不絕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Xinghe they sent the envoy Shijiuyun and others with local products as tribute; down to Wuding it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Xinghe they sent the envoy Shijiuyun and others with local tribute, and envoys continued without break down to the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 失韋國，在勿吉北千里，去洛六千里。

translations.literal: The state of Shiwei lies a thousand li north of Wuji and six thousand li from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Shiwei lies a thousand li north of Wuji and six thousand li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 路出和龍北千餘里，入契丹國，又北行十日至啜水，又北行三日有蓋水，又北行三日有犢了山，其山高大，周回三百餘里，又北行三日有大水名屈利，又北行三日至刃水，又北行五日到其國。

translations.literal: The route goes out more than a thousand li north of Helong, enters the Khitan state, goes north again ten days to the Chuo River, north again three days to the Gai River, north again three days to Mount Duliao, the mountain high and great, circling more than three hundred li; north again three days to a great river named Quli; north again three days to the Ren River; north again five days to their state.
translations.idiomatic: The route runs more than a thousand li north of Helong into Khitan territory, then ten days north to the Chuo River, three days north to the Gai River, three days north to lofty Mount Duliao, which circles more than three hundred li, three days north to the great Quli River, three days north to the Ren River, and five days north to their country.

sentences.zh: 有大水從北而來，廣四里餘，名㮈水。

translations.literal: A great river comes from the north, more than four li wide, named the Nu River.
translations.idiomatic: A great river flows from the north, more than four li wide, called the Nu River.

sentences.zh: 國土下濕。

translations.literal: The state's land is low and wet.
translations.idiomatic: Their land is low and damp.

sentences.zh: 語與庫莫奚、契丹、豆莫婁國同。

translations.literal: Their language is the same as that of Kumo Xi, Khitan, and Doumolou.
translations.idiomatic: Their language is the same as that of the Kumo Xi, Khitan, and Doumolou.

sentences.zh: 頗有粟麥及穄，唯食猪魚，養牛馬，俗又無羊。

translations.literal: They have rather much millet, wheat, and broomcorn millet; they eat only pork and fish, raise cattle and horses, and by custom again have no sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They grow millet, wheat, and broomcorn millet, eat chiefly pork and fish, raise cattle and horses, and by custom keep no sheep.

sentences.zh: 夏則城居，冬逐水草。

translations.literal: In summer they dwell in walled settlements; in winter they follow water and grass.
translations.idiomatic: In summer they live in walled settlements; in winter they follow the pastures.

sentences.zh: 亦多貂皮。

translations.literal: They also have much sable fur.
translations.idiomatic: They also produce much sable fur.

sentences.zh: 丈夫索髮。

translations.literal: Husbands plait their hair.
translations.idiomatic: Men wear their hair in braids.

sentences.zh: 用角弓，其箭尤長。

translations.literal: They use horn bows; their arrows are especially long.
translations.idiomatic: They use horn bows, and their arrows are especially long.

sentences.zh: 女婦束髮，作叉手髻。

translations.literal: Women bind their hair and make a crossed-hands bun.
translations.idiomatic: Women bind their hair into a crossed-hands bun.

sentences.zh: 其國少竊盜，盜一徵三，殺人者責馬三百匹。

translations.literal: Their state has little theft; for one theft threefold is levied; for killing a man three hundred horses are exacted.
translations.idiomatic: Theft is rare among them: one theft draws a threefold penalty, and murder is punished with a fine of three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 男女悉衣白鹿皮襦袴。

translations.literal: Men and women all wear jackets and trousers of white deerskin.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike dress in jackets and trousers of white deerskin.

sentences.zh: 有麴釀酒。

translations.literal: They have yeast to brew wine.
translations.idiomatic: They brew wine with yeast.

sentences.zh: 俗愛赤珠，為婦人飾，穿挂於頸，以多為貴，女不得此，乃至不嫁。

translations.literal: Their custom loves red pearls as women's ornament, strung and hung at the neck; the more the more honored; a woman who does not obtain these may even go unmarried.
translations.idiomatic: They prize red pearls as women's ornaments, strung about the neck—the more the better. A woman without them might not marry at all.

sentences.zh: 父母死，男女眾哭三年，屍則置於林樹之上。

translations.literal: When parents die, men and women all wail together for three years; the corpse is then placed atop trees in the forest.
translations.idiomatic: When parents die, the whole community mourns for three years, and the corpse is placed in the forest treetops.

sentences.zh: 武定二年四月，始遣使張焉豆伐等獻其方物，迄武定末，貢使相尋。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Wuding they first sent the envoy Zhang Yandoufa and others to present local products; down to the end of Wuding tribute envoys followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Wuding they first sent the envoy Zhang Yandoufa and others with local tribute, and envoys continued in succession down to the end of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 豆莫婁國，在勿吉國北千里，去洛六千里，舊北扶餘也。

translations.literal: The state of Doumolou lies a thousand li north of Wuji, six thousand li from Luoyang; it is old northern Buyeo.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Doumolou lies a thousand li north of Wuji and six thousand li from Luoyang, in the territory of old northern Buyeo.

sentences.zh: 在失韋之東，東至於海，方二千里。

translations.literal: It lies east of Shiwei, eastward to the sea, two thousand li square.
translations.idiomatic: It lies east of Shiwei, reaching east to the sea, and measures two thousand li square.

sentences.zh: 其人土著，有宮室倉庫。

translations.literal: Its people are settled natives and have palaces and storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: The people are native settlers with palaces and storehouses.

sentences.zh: 多山陵廣澤，於東夷之域最為平敞。

translations.literal: There are many hills and broad marshes; within the domain of the Eastern Yi it is the most level and open.
translations.idiomatic: The land has many hills and broad marshes and is the most level and open country in the Eastern Yi region.

sentences.zh: 地宜五穀，不生五果。

translations.literal: The soil suits the five grains; it does not produce the five fruits.
translations.idiomatic: The soil is good for the five grains but does not bear the five fruits.

sentences.zh: 其人長大，性強勇，謹厚，不寇抄。

translations.literal: Its people are tall and large, by nature strong and brave, careful and thick, and do not raid or plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The people are tall and sturdy, brave by nature, sober and honest, and do not raid or plunder.

sentences.zh: 其君長皆以六畜名官，邑落有豪帥。

translations.literal: Their rulers and chiefs all take the six domestic animals as names for offices; settlements and hamlets have powerful leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Their rulers name their offices after the six domestic animals, and each settlement has its powerful headmen.

sentences.zh: 飲食亦用俎豆。

translations.literal: In eating and drinking they also use platters and stands.
translations.idiomatic: They also eat from platters and stands.

sentences.zh: 有麻布衣，制類高麗而幅大，其國大人，以金銀飾之。

translations.literal: They have hempen cloth garments, made like Goryeo's but with broader panels; the great men of the state adorn them with gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: They weave hemp cloth garments similar to Goryeo's but broader in cut, and their great men adorn them with gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 用刑嚴急，殺人者死，沒其家人為奴婢。

translations.literal: They apply punishments sternly and urgently; killers die, and their families are confiscated as male and female slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Their punishments are harsh: murderers are put to death and their families enslaved.

sentences.zh: 俗淫，尤惡妬婦，妬者殺之，尸其國南山上至腐。

translations.literal: Their customs are licentious; they especially hate jealous wives; jealous ones are killed and their corpses exposed on the southern mountain of the state until they rot.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs are loose, and they especially despise jealous wives, whom they kill and leave exposed on the southern mountain until the bodies rot.

sentences.zh: 女家欲得，輸牛馬乃與之。

translations.literal: If the bride's family wishes to obtain her, they deliver cattle and horses and only then is she given.
translations.idiomatic: The bride's family must deliver cattle and horses before she is given in marriage.

sentences.zh: 或言本穢貊之地也。

translations.literal: Some say it was originally the land of the Huimo.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the land was originally that of the Huimo.

sentences.zh: 地豆于國，[5]在失韋西千餘里。

translations.literal: The state of Didouyu[5] lies more than a thousand li west of Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Didouyu[5] lies more than a thousand li west of Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 多牛羊，出名馬，皮為衣服，無五穀，惟食肉酪。

translations.literal: They have many cattle and sheep and produce famed horses; skins serve as clothing; they have no five grains and eat only meat and curds.
translations.idiomatic: They keep many cattle and sheep and breed famed horses, dress in hides, grow no grain, and live on meat and dairy alone.

sentences.zh: 延興二年八月，遣使朝貢，至于太和六年，貢使不絕。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Yanxing they sent envoys to court with tribute; down to the sixth year of Taihe tribute envoys did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Yanxing they sent envoys to court, and tribute missions continued without break down to the sixth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 十四年，頻來犯塞，高祖詔征西大將軍、陽平王頤擊走之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year they frequently came to violate the frontier; Emperor Gaozu edicted the General Who Conquers the West, the Prince of Yangping Yi, to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year they raided the frontier repeatedly. Emperor Gaozu ordered the General Who Conquers the West, the Prince of Yangping, Yi, to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 自後時朝京師，迄武定末，貢使不絕。

translations.literal: From then on they periodically came to the capital; down to the end of Wuding tribute envoys did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they came periodically to the capital, and tribute envoys continued without break down to the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 庫莫奚國之先，東部宇文之別種也。

translations.literal: The forebears of the state of Kumo Xi were a separate branch of the Eastern Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: The Kumo Xi were originally a branch of the Eastern Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 初為慕容元真所破，遺落者竄匿松漠之間。

translations.literal: At first they were broken by Murong Yuanzhen; those left behind fled and hid among the pine deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yuanzhen first defeated them, and the survivors fled into the pine deserts.

sentences.zh: 其民不潔淨，而善射獵，好為寇鈔。

translations.literal: Their people are not clean, yet are skilled in archery and hunting and love to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: They are not fastidious in their habits, but are skilled hunters and fond of raiding.

sentences.zh: 登國三年，太祖親自出討，至弱洛水南，大破之，獲其四部落，馬牛羊豕十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dengguo Taizu personally went out to punish them, reaching south of the Ruoluo River, routed them greatly, and captured their four tribal groups, with more than a hundred thousand horses, cattle, sheep, and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dengguo, Taizu campaigned against them in person, routed them south of the Ruoluo River, and captured four tribes together with more than a hundred thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此羣狄諸種不識德義，互相侵盜，有犯王略，故往征之。
