translations.literal: The Emperor said: "These various Di peoples do not know virtue and righteousness, rob one another, and violate the royal domain, and so We went to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "These tribes know neither virtue nor righteousness. They plunder one another and violate the imperial domain, and that is why We marched against them.

sentences.zh: 且鼠竊狗盜，何足為患。

translations.literal: Moreover rats stealing and dogs thieving—what worth as a calamity?
translations.idiomatic: Mere rat-thieves and dog-bandits are hardly worth Our concern.

sentences.zh: 今中州大亂，吾先平之，然後張其威懷，則無所不服矣。

translations.literal: Now the central provinces are in great disorder; We shall first pacify them, and then extend awe and cherishing, and nothing will fail to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The central provinces are in turmoil. We shall pacify them first, and then extend Our majesty and kindness, and none will fail to submit.

sentences.zh: 」既而車駕南還雲中，懷服燕趙。

translations.literal: " Thereafter the imperial carriage returned south to Yunzhong, and Yan and Zhao submitted in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter the imperial carriage returned south to Yunzhong, and Yan and Zhao submitted in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 十數年間，諸種與庫莫奚亦皆滋盛。

translations.literal: Within a dozen years or so the various peoples together with Kumo Xi all likewise grew abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Within a dozen years the various tribes, Kumo Xi included, all grew strong again.

sentences.zh: 及開遼海，置戍和龍，諸夷震懼，各獻方物。

translations.literal: When Liaohai was opened and garrisons set at Helong, the various Yi were shaken with fear and each presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaohai was opened and garrisons placed at Helong, the frontier peoples were awed into submission and each presented local tribute.

sentences.zh: 高宗、顯祖世，庫莫奚歲致名馬文皮。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Emperor Gaozong and Emperor Xianzu, Kumo Xi each year presented famed horses and patterned pelts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Gaozong and Xianzu, Kumo Xi presented famed horses and patterned furs every year.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu they sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Gaozu they sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，輒入塞內，辭以畏地豆于鈔掠，詔書切責之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe they repeatedly entered within the passes, pleading that they feared plunder by Didouyu; an edict sternly rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe they repeatedly entered the frontier passes, claiming fear of raids by Didouyu. An edict sternly rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，入寇安州，營燕幽三州兵數千人擊走之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year they invaded Anzhou; troops of several thousand from the garrisons of Yan, You, and the three provinces struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year they raided Anzhou and were driven off by several thousand troops from the Yan and You garrisons.

sentences.zh: 後復款附，每求入塞，與民交易。

translations.literal: Later they again submitted sincerely and each time asked to enter the passes to trade with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Later they submitted again and repeatedly asked to enter the passes to trade with the people.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔曰：「庫莫奚去太和二十一年以前，與安營二州邊民參居，交易往來，並無疑貳。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong edicted: "Kumo Xi before the twenty-first year of Taihe lived intermingled with the frontier people of An and Ying, traded back and forth, and had no doubts or divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong edicted, "Before the twenty-first year of Taihe, Kumo Xi lived among the frontier people of An and Ying, traded freely, and gave no cause for suspicion.

sentences.zh: 至二十二年叛逆以來，遂爾遠竄。

translations.literal: From the twenty-second year, since their rebellion, they then fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Since their rebellion in the twenty-second year, they have fled far away.

sentences.zh: 今雖款附，猶在塞表，每請入塞與民交易。

translations.literal: Now though they submit sincerely they are still beyond the passes and each time ask to enter the passes to trade with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Though they have submitted again, they remain beyond the passes and repeatedly ask to enter and trade with the people.

sentences.zh: 若抑而不許，乖其歸向之心；

translations.literal: If We restrain and do not permit it, We thwart their hearts of turning toward Us.
translations.idiomatic: To refuse them would thwart their desire to submit.

sentences.zh: 聽而不虞，或有萬一之警。

translations.literal: If We hear and do not guard against it, there may be alarm in one case out of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to permit them without precaution may invite unforeseen trouble.

sentences.zh: 不容依先任其交易，事宜限節，交市之日，州遣上佐監之。

translations.literal: It is not permitted to follow the former practice and allow their trade without limit; affairs should be restricted and regulated; on the day of market exchange the province shall send a senior aide to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: They may no longer trade as freely as before. The exchange must be regulated, and on market days the province shall send a senior official to supervise.

sentences.zh: 」自是已後，歲常朝獻，至於武定末不絕。

translations.literal: " From then on they annually presented tribute at court, and down to the end of Wuding it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter they presented tribute every year without break down to the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 契丹國，在庫莫奚東，異種同類，俱竄於松漠之間。

translations.literal: The state of Khitan lies east of Kumo Xi; a different lineage but the same kind, both hiding in the pine deserts.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan state lies east of Kumo Xi. Though a distinct lineage, they are kin, and both took refuge in the pine deserts.

sentences.zh: 登國中，國軍大破之，遂逃迸，與庫莫奚分背。

translations.literal: In the Dengguo era the state's army routed them greatly; they then fled in disorder and separated from Kumo Xi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dengguo era the imperial army routed them, and they fled in disorder, separating from the Kumo Xi.

sentences.zh: 經數十年，稍滋蔓，有部落，於和龍之北數百里，多為寇盜。

translations.literal: After several decades they gradually spread; they had tribal groups several hundred li north of Helong and mostly acted as raiders and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: After several decades they gradually spread, forming tribes several hundred li north of Helong that mostly raided and plundered.

sentences.zh: 真君以來，求朝獻，歲貢名馬。

translations.literal: From Zhenjun onward they sought to present tribute at court and each year presented famed horses.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhenjun era onward they sought audience at court and presented famed horses each year.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，使莫弗紇何辰奉獻，得班饗於諸國之末。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xianzu the envoy Mofuhe Hechen presented tribute and was granted a place in the feast at the end of the various states.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzu the envoy Mofuhe Hechen presented tribute and was granted a place at the feast, though last among the states.

sentences.zh: 歸而相謂，言國家之美，心皆忻慕，於是東北羣狄聞之，莫不思服。

translations.literal: Returning they said to one another, speaking of the state's beauty; all their hearts rejoiced and admired, and then the Di peoples of the northeast, hearing of it, none failed to think of submission.
translations.idiomatic: On returning they spoke to one another of the splendor of the state, and all were filled with admiration. When the tribes of the northeast heard of it, none failed to think of submission.

sentences.zh: 悉萬丹部、何大何部、伏弗郁部、羽陵部、[6]日連部、匹絜部、黎部、[7]吐六于部等，[8]各以其名馬文皮入獻天府，遂求為常。

translations.literal: The Xiwandan, Hedahé, Fufuyu, Yuling,[6] Rilian, Pijie, Li,[7] Tuliuyu,[8] and other divisions each with their famed horses and patterned pelts entered tribute at the celestial treasury and then asked that it become regular.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiwandan, Hedahé, Fufuyu, Yuling,[6] Rilian, Pijie, Li,[7] Tuliuyu,[8] and other divisions each presented famed horses and patterned furs to the imperial treasury and asked to make the practice regular.

sentences.zh: 皆得交市於和龍、密雲之間，貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: All were able to trade at markets between Helong and Miyun; tribute did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: They were all permitted to trade between Helong and Miyun, and tribute continued without break.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，高句麗竊與蠕蠕謀，欲取地豆于以分之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe Goguryeo secretly plotted with the Rouran, wishing to take Didouyu and divide it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe, Goguryeo secretly plotted with the Rouran to seize Didouyu and divide its territory.

sentences.zh: 契丹懼其侵軼，其莫弗賀勿于率其部落車三千乘、眾萬餘口，驅徙雜畜，求入內附，止於白狼水東。

translations.literal: The Khitan feared encroachment and violation; their Mofu Hewuyu led their tribal group with three thousand carts and more than ten thousand mouths, driving mixed livestock, sought to enter and attach inward, and halted east of the White Wolf River.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan, fearing invasion, were led by their chief Hewuyu with three thousand carts and more than ten thousand people, driving their herds, to seek refuge within the empire. They halted east of the White Wolf River.

sentences.zh: 自此歲常朝貢。

translations.literal: From then on they annually presented tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: From that time they presented tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 後告饑，高祖矜之，聽其入關市糴。

translations.literal: Later they reported famine; Emperor Gaozu pitied them and permitted them to enter the passes to buy grain at market.
translations.idiomatic: Later they reported famine. Emperor Gaozu took pity on them and allowed them to enter the passes to buy grain.

sentences.zh: 及世宗、肅宗時，恒遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: By the times of Emperor Shizong and Emperor Suzong they constantly sent envoys to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Shizong and Suzong they regularly sent envoys with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，契丹使人祖真等三十人還，靈太后以其俗嫁娶之際，以青氊為上服，人給青氊兩匹，賞其誠款之心，餘依舊式。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era the Khitan envoy Zuzhen and thirty others returned; Empress Dowager Ling, because in their custom at marriage they take blue felt as upper garment, gave each person two bolts of blue felt to reward their sincere hearts; the rest followed the old forms.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiping era, when the Khitan envoy Zuzhen and thirty others returned home, Empress Dowager Ling, knowing that blue felt was their ceremonial dress at weddings, gave each man two bolts of blue felt to reward their sincerity. The rest followed the usual forms.

sentences.zh: 朝貢至齊受禪常不絕。

translations.literal: Tribute at court continued without break down to Qi receiving the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute missions continued without break down to the Qi succession.

sentences.zh: 烏洛侯國，在地豆于之北，去代都四千五百餘里。

translations.literal: The state of Wuluohou lies north of Didouyu, more than four thousand five hundred li from the capital at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Wuluohou lies north of Didouyu, more than four thousand five hundred li from the capital at Dai.

sentences.zh: 其土下濕，多霧氣而寒，民冬則穿地為室，夏則隨原阜畜牧。

translations.literal: Its soil is low and wet, with much fog and cold; the people in winter bore into the earth for chambers, in summer follow hills and mounds to pasture livestock.
translations.idiomatic: The land is low, damp, foggy, and cold. In winter the people dig pit dwellings; in summer they pasture their herds on the hills.

sentences.zh: 多豕，有穀麥。

translations.literal: They have many pigs and have grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: They keep many pigs and grow grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 無大君長，部落莫弗皆世為之。

translations.literal: They have no great ruler or chief; tribal Mofu are all hereditary in office.
translations.idiomatic: They have no paramount ruler; tribal chiefs hold office by hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 其俗繩髮，皮服，以珠為飾。

translations.literal: Their custom is to bind the hair, wear hides, and use pearls for ornament.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they bind their hair, dress in hides, and adorn themselves with pearls.

sentences.zh: 民尚勇，不為姦竊，故慢藏野積而無寇盜。

translations.literal: The people esteem courage and do not commit adultery or theft; therefore they store goods carelessly in the open wild and have no robbers or thieves.
translations.idiomatic: The people value courage and do not steal, so goods are left openly in the fields without fear of thieves.

sentences.zh: 好獵射。

translations.literal: They love hunting and archery.
translations.idiomatic: They love hunting and archery.

sentences.zh: 樂有箜篌，木槽革面而施九弦。

translations.literal: In music they have the konghou, a wooden trough with leather face and nine strings set upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Their music includes the konghou, a wooden trough covered with leather and strung with nine strings.

sentences.zh: 其國西北有完水，東北流合于難水，其地小水皆注於難，東入于海。

translations.literal: Northwest of their state is the Wan River, flowing northeast to join the Nan River; the small waters of their land all pour into the Nan and enter the sea to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of their country is the Wan River, which flows northeast to join the Nan River. The lesser streams of their land all feed the Nan and reach the sea to the east.

sentences.zh: 又西北二十日行有于巳尼大水，所謂北海也。

translations.literal: Again, twenty days' travel northwest is the great Yusini water, what is called the Northern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days' travel northwest lies the great Yusini Sea, called the Northern Sea.

sentences.zh: 世祖真君四年來朝，稱其國西北有國家先帝舊墟，石室南北九十步，東西四十步，高七十尺，室有神靈，民多祈請。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenjun, Emperor Shizu, they came to court, saying that northwest of their state was an old site of the state's Former Emperor, a stone chamber ninety paces north-south, forty paces east-west, seventy feet high; the chamber had a numinous spirit and the people made many prayers and requests.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenjun they came to court and reported that northwest of their country stood an ancient site of the imperial ancestors: a stone chamber ninety paces north to south, forty east to west, and seventy feet high, inhabited by a numinous presence to whom the people prayed.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣中書侍郎李敞告祭焉，刊祝文於室之壁而還。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu sent Palace Gentleman Li Chang to announce sacrifice there, carved a prayer text on the chamber's wall, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu sent Palace Gentleman Li Chang to perform the sacrifice, inscribed a prayer on the chamber wall, and returned.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夷狄之於中國，羈縻而已。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Barbarian Di toward the Middle Kingdom are only held by loose reins.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: Toward the Middle Kingdom, the frontier peoples were held only by loose reins.

sentences.zh: 高麗歲修貢職，東藩之冠，榮哀之禮，致自天朝，亦為優矣。

translations.literal: Goryeo yearly performed tribute duties, the crown of the eastern frontier; the rites of glory and mourning sent from the celestial court were also generous.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo performed annual tribute and stood foremost among the eastern frontier states. That mourning honors should come from the celestial court was generosity indeed.

sentences.zh: 其他碌碌，咸知款貢，豈牛馬內向，東風入律者也。

translations.literal: The others, numerous and humble, all knew sincere tribute—was it that cattle and horses turned inward and the eastern wind entered the pitch pipes?
translations.idiomatic: The others, numerous though they were, all knew how to offer sincere tribute. Was this truly a case of cattle and horses turning homeward and the eastern wind falling into tune with the pitch pipes?

sentences.zh: 魏正始中入寇遼西安平 三國魏志卷三０東夷傳、隋書卷八一高麗傳「遼西安平」作「西安平」。

translations.literal: In Wei's Zhengshi era invasion of Liaoxi Anping: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Wei Annals 30 Eastern Yi Account and History of the Sui 81 Goryeo Account write "Liaoxi Anping" as "Xi'anping."
translations.idiomatic: On the Zhengshi-era raid on Liaoxi Anping: the Eastern Yi account in Wei Annals 30 of the Records of the Three Kingdoms and Goryeo account in History of the Sui 81 read "Xi'anping" rather than "Liaoxi Anping."

sentences.zh: 按後漢書郡國志二安平國屬冀州，志五，西安平屬幽州遼東郡。

translations.literal: According to the Treatise on Commanderies and States 2 of the History of the Later Han, Anping State belonged to Jizhou; Treatise 5: Xi'anping belonged to Youzhou, Liaodong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Treatise on Commanderies and States in the History of the Later Han, Anping State belonged to Jizhou, while Xi'anping belonged to Liaodong Commandery in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 遼西郡沒有安平或西安平縣。

translations.literal: Liaoxi Commandery had neither Anping nor Xi'anping counties.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi Commandery had neither an Anping nor an Xi'anping county.

sentences.zh: 這裏「遼」字衍，或「遼」下脫「東」字。

translations.literal: Here the character "Liao" is superfluous, or the character "dong" has dropped below "Liao."
translations.idiomatic: Here the character for "Liao" appears to be superfluous, or the character for "east" has been lost after "Liao."

sentences.zh: 正始中世宗於東堂引見其使芮悉弗 諸本「宗」作「祖」，北史卷九四高麗傳作「宣武」。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi Emperor Shizong at the Eastern Hall received his envoy Ruixifu: various editions write "Zong" as "Zu"; History of the North 94 Goryeo Account writes "Xuanwu."
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Shizong receiving the envoy Ruixifu at the Eastern Hall in Zhengshi: various editions read "Zong" as "Zu," and the Goryeo account in History of the North 94 has "Xuanwu."

sentences.zh: 按上稱「正始」年號，自當作「世宗」，北史例稱帝號。

translations.literal: According to the above, since the era title "Zhengshi" is used, it should read "Emperor Shizong"; the History of the North regularly uses imperial titles.
translations.idiomatic: Since the era title Zhengshi is used above, the reference should be to Emperor Shizong; the History of the North regularly uses reign titles rather than temple names.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 具弗伏國 按卷六顯祖紀皇興元年二月、二年四月兩見此部，都作「具伏弗」。

translations.literal: State of Jufufu: according to Basic Annals 6, Emperor Xianzu's records, second month of the first year of Huangxing and fourth month of the second year both see this division, all written "Jufufu."
translations.idiomatic: On the state of Jufufu: Basic Annals 6 records this tribe in the second month of Huangxing 1 and the fourth month of Huangxing 2, both times as "Jufufu."

sentences.zh: 下契丹傳有「伏弗郁部」，上脫「具」字，又「郁」「部」二字倒誤，但也可證這裏「弗伏」當作「伏弗」。

translations.literal: Below, the Khitan account has "Fufuyu Division"; above the character "Ju" is missing, and again the two characters "Yu" and "bu" are reversed in error, but this also can prove that here "Fufu" should be "Fufu."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan account below has "Fufuyu Division," showing that "Ju" is missing above and that "yu" and "bu" are reversed. This also confirms that "fufu" here should read "fufu."

sentences.zh: 拔大何國 按下契丹傳有「何大何部」，卷六顯祖紀皇興二年四月作「阿大何」。

translations.literal: State of Badahé: according to the Khitan account below there is "Hedahé Division"; Basic Annals 6, fourth month of the second year of Huangxing writes "Adahé."
translations.idiomatic: On the state of Badahé: the Khitan account below has "Hedahé Division," and Basic Annals 6, fourth month of Huangxing 2, reads "Adahé."

sentences.zh: 這裏「拔」字當是「何」或「阿」之訛。

translations.literal: Here the character "Ba" should be a corruption of "He" or "A."
translations.idiomatic: Here the character "ba" is likely a corruption of "he" or "a."

sentences.zh: 地豆于國 北史卷九四「于」作「干」。

translations.literal: State of Didouyu: History of the North 94 writes "yu" as "gan."
translations.idiomatic: On the state of Didouyu: History of the North 94 writes the final character as "gan" rather than "yu."

sentences.zh: 按本書他處也多作「地豆于」，間亦作「干」，北史則多作「干」，間作「于」，今仍之。

translations.literal: According to this book elsewhere it is also mostly written "Didouyu," occasionally "gan"; the History of the North mostly writes "gan," occasionally "yu"; the present text is retained as is.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere in this book the name appears mostly as Didouyu and occasionally as Didougan; the History of the North mostly has Didougan and occasionally Didouyu. The present text is retained as it stands.

sentences.zh: 伏弗郁部羽陵部 按上勿吉傳見「具弗伏國」、「郁羽陵國」，卷六顯祖紀皇興元年二月、二年四月並見「具伏弗、郁羽陵」，這裏「伏弗」上當脫「具」字，「郁」「部」誤倒，當作「具伏弗部、郁羽陵部」。

translations.literal: Fufuyu Division, Yuling Division: according to the Wuji account above there are "Jufufu State" and "Yuyuling State"; Basic Annals 6, second month of Huangxing 1 and fourth month of Huangxing 2 both see "Jufufu, Yuyuling"; here above "Fufu" the character "Ju" should be missing, "Yu" and "bu" are wrongly reversed, and it should read "Jufufu Division, Yuyuling Division."
translations.idiomatic: On Fufuyu Division and Yuling Division: the Wuji account above has "Jufufu State" and "Yuyuling State," and Basic Annals 6 records "Jufufu" and "Yuyuling" in Huangxing 1.2 and 2.4. Here "ju" is missing before "fufu," and "yu" and "bu" are reversed; the text should read "Jufufu Division, Yuyuling Division."

sentences.zh: 匹絜部黎部 按上勿吉傳及卷六顯祖紀皇興元年、二年並見「匹黎尒部」，通典卷二００契丹條作「匹黎部」。

translations.literal: Pijie Division, Li Division: according to the Wuji account above and Basic Annals 6, Huangxing years 1 and 2, all see "Pilier Division"; Tongdian 200 Khitan entry writes "Pili Division."
translations.idiomatic: On Pijie Division and Li Division: the Wuji account above and Basic Annals 6 for Huangxing 1 and 2 have "Pilier Division," while Tongdian 200, Khitan entry, has "Pili Division."

sentences.zh: 疑這裏「匹絜」下衍「部」字，本作「匹絜黎部」，誤分二部。

translations.literal: It is suspected that here below "Pijie" the character "bu" is superfluous; originally it was "Pijieli Division," wrongly divided into two divisions.
translations.idiomatic: It is likely that the character for "division" after "Pijie" is superfluous and that the original reading was "Pijieli Division," wrongly split into two divisions.

sentences.zh: 吐六于部 北史卷九四契丹傳「于」作「干」，卷六顯祖紀皇興二年四月作「叱六手」，通典卷二００作「比六干」。

translations.literal: Tuliuyu Division: History of the North 94 Khitan Account writes "yu" as "gan"; Basic Annals 6, fourth month of Huangxing 2 writes "Chiliushou"; Tongdian 200 writes "Biliugan."
translations.idiomatic: On Tuliuyu Division: History of the North 94, Khitan account, has "gan" for "yu"; Basic Annals 6, Huangxing 2.4, has "Chiliushou"; and Tongdian 200 has "Biliugan."

sentences.zh: 疑「吐」「比」皆「叱」字之訛。

translations.literal: It is suspected that both "Tu" and "Bi" are corruptions of the character "Chi."
translations.idiomatic: Both "tu" and "bi" are likely corruptions of "chi."

sentences.zh: 「手」顯訛，「于」「干」不知孰是。

translations.literal: The character "shou" is clearly erroneous; whether "yu" or "gan" is correct is not known.
translations.idiomatic: "Shou" is clearly erroneous; whether "yu" or "gan" is correct remains uncertain.
